prize_parts.citation: For the theory of the Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep B036 as my preferred configuration, but with less certainty on credit than in round 1. The scientific core is unchanged. Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant insulators, a bulk integer that guarantees protected boundary states and that the 2016 prize, built on the integer quantum Hall class and the Haldane model, did not cover. Molenkamp's group then measured the quantized edge conductance in HgTe within two years, and independent transport and ARPES work in several material families has confirmed the picture for more than fifteen years. Theory can also explain it quantitatively: band inversion and spin-orbit coupling in HgTe and Bi-based compounds are reproduced by first-principles calculations, which is the kind of verified link between prediction, calculation and measurement that I weigh most. The concept has spread to photonics, cold atoms and phononics. I regard this as a new state of matter, not a better instrument, and that is how I weigh it against B025.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real and the exchange has made it sharper, not smaller. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the specific HgTe prediction that Molenkamp tested, Zhang is deceased, and Bernevig and Hughes are alive and not in the trio. The three-dimensional work of Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Roy and Hasan is also outside it. Pearce is right that a prize leaving out the prediction that the experiment tested would be contested, and I cannot claim the trio is beyond argument. The subject overlap with the 2016 prize also remains an objection that a citation can reduce but not remove. By contrast, B025 has four supporters naming identical laureates, a settled maturity record, and a cleaner credit story, and its supporters themselves list B036 only as an alternative. I do not dismiss that. I hold my preference because I rank a new class of matter above a measurement capability, not because I think B025 is weak.

responses.point: Pearce keeps B036 as first alternative but says the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D work is the sharper vulnerability, and asks whether the committee can defend the trio as it stands.
responses.response: I can defend it as a choice, not as a complete account. Kane and Mele supply the invariant and the prediction of the effect as a new class, and Molenkamp supplies the observation. The HgTe-specific prediction of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is what made the experiment possible, so I would not call the omission a technicality. My answer is that the citation should be written for the Z2 invariant and the observed state, and that the expert report should settle whether the BHZ proposal is the decisive step. If the experts judge that the prediction of the HgTe effect and the Z2 theory cannot be separated, I would accept moving to B025 rather than stretching the three-name limit. I will not support a trio the experts cannot defend.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B025 for its clean two-name credit, many independent replications and concrete downstream uses, and asks whether the Katori and Ye pair is the most natural attribution on the table.
responses.response: I agree that Katori and Ye is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and the Hall mentor link you disclosed looks to me like a matter for disclosure rather than recusal, though that is for the Chair. Our remaining difference is about what the prize recognises. I accept that the lattice clock is not a minor refinement, but the 10^-18 result so far delivers capability and bounds rather than a new fact about nature. Your remark that Ye's clocks depend on the frequency comb also keeps the 2005 overlap alive in my mind. If the committee ranks a mature, cleanly credited measurement revolution first, I would vote for it without reluctance.

responses.point: Mehlig frames the essential idea as the Z2 invariant and the bulk-boundary correspondence for time-reversal-invariant insulators, and says the committee must be ready to explain why Bernevig and Hughes are not named.
responses.response: I accept your framing and have moved my citation toward it, with the Z2 theory first and the HgTe observation second. You are also right that I called the triad natural too easily in round 1. The explanation for the omission has to be written down before the vote, not improvised afterwards. In my reading the explanation is that the invariant and the first observation define the discovery, and the HgTe prediction is a step that connects them. I admit that is an argument a colleague can reject. On the 3D work, I still would not add Fu or Hasan, because the cap forces a choice and the 2D state is the conceptual origin.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B025 first as a settled result built on atomic structure, and says she defers to Mehlig and me on how serious the B036 priority questions are, while seeing B036 as a strong second choice.
responses.response: Thank you for deferring to me on the condensed-matter priority questions, and I will answer with the following judgment: they are serious. I do not think B036 is ahead of the clock on credit, and I say so plainly. Where I differ is that I would not describe the clock as the safer choice on discovery grounds. Your point that the light shift cancels at the magic wavelength and the evaluation is reproduced across laboratories is the type of verification I respect, and I cannot add to your judgement on the blackbody and lattice light-shift budget. I only ask that the committee does not treat the absence of any revision risk as the same thing as scientific priority.

responses.point: Olsson says the TEM and STEM corrector claims are separate inventions, asks the experts for dates, and says she would not block B025 and would move to it if the priority of the first Sr lattice-clock demonstration is confirmed.
responses.response: Thank you for separating the TEM and STEM lines so clearly. That confirms what I feared about B008: two credible inventions cannot be covered by three names without a visible gap. I note that you would move to B025 on the priority question, which is the same open point several of us have raised. I think the committee needs the experts' dates for the first Sr lattice clock demonstration before the vote, because that settles whether Takamoto belongs next to Katori and whether the pair is stable.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports find the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction separable from the Kane-Mele Z2 theory; if they do not, the trio in B036 is hard to defend.
Whether a citation centred on the Z2 invariant and the HgTe quantum spin Hall state is distinct enough from the 2016 prize for topological phases.
Whether Takamoto, Lemonde or other groups have an early priority claim on the Sr lattice clock that would change the B025 pair or its citation.
Whether the committee will treat a lattice clock at 10^-18 as a discovery or as enabling metrology, and how much that matters against its cleaner credit.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name for B036 or B025 is apparent from my profile. Kroll's disclosure of a Hall mentor lineage for B025 does not concern me. My own work in electronic-structure theory of spin-orbit and band-inverted materials is related in method to B036, but I have no collaboration or mentor link to Kane, Mele or Molenkamp, and I would flag any such link.
